knowledge:
- key_parameters: sce=SingleCellExperiment object containing the real cells experiment ;; sce_bead=SingleCellExperiment object containing the single-stained beads experiment ;; marker_to_barc=A data frame or tibble mapping the channel names (markers) to their corresponding barcodes used in the beads experiment ;; impute_value=Value used for imputation (typically NA) ;; overwrite=Logical indicating whether to overwrite existing assays in the SCE object (typically FALSE)
- alternatives: CATALYST (specifically computeSpillmat / Chevrier et al. 2018 method) which relies on estimating a spillover matrix using non-negative matrix factorization. spillR is preferred when you want to directly describe spillover channels and true signals using a mixture of nonparametric distributions, assuming the spillover distribution itself carries over to the biological experiment.
- when_to_use: When analyzing mass cytometry (CyTOF) data where channel interference (spillover) is present and a corresponding single-stained bead experiment is available to estimate spillover.
- pitfalls: If the target marker in the beads experiment does not overlap with the real cells, it indicates a low-quality bead experiment, which can lead to unreliable spillover estimation. Ensure the mapping table (marker_to_barc) correctly maps the channel names to the exact barcodes used in the beads experiment.

workflows.name: cytof_spillover_compensation
workflows.intent: Compensate for channel spillover in mass cytometry data using a nonparametric finite mixture model estimated from single-stained beads.
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare bead and cell data using CATALYST and map markers to barcodes ;; 2. Perform spillover compensation using spillR::compCytof ;; 3. Generate diagnostic plots using spillR::plotDiagnostics to evaluate the compensation.
workflows.code:
library(spillR)
library(CATALYST)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

bc_key <- c(139, 141:156, 158:176)
sce_bead <- prepData(ss_exp)
sce_bead <- assignPrelim(sce_bead, bc_key, verbose = FALSE)
sce_bead <- applyCutoffs(estCutoffs(sce_bead))
sce_bead <- computeSpillmat(sce_bead)

# --------- experiment with real cells ---------
data(mp_cells, package = "CATALYST")
sce <- prepData(mp_cells)

# --------- table for mapping markers and barcode ---------
marker_to_barc <-
    rowData(sce_bead)[, c("channel_name", "is_bc")] |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::filter(is_bc == TRUE) |>
    mutate(barcode = bc_key) |>
    select(marker = channel_name, barcode)

# --------- compensate function from spillR package ---------
sce_spillr <-
    spillR::compCytof(sce, sce_bead, marker_to_barc, impute_value = NA, 
                      overwrite = FALSE)

# --------- 2d histogram from CATALYST package -------
as <- c("counts", "exprs", "compcounts", "compexprs")
chs <- c("Yb171Di", "Yb173Di")
ps <- lapply(as, function(a) plotScatter(sce_spillr, chs, assay = a))
plot_grid(plotlist = ps, nrow = 2)

ps <- spillR::plotDiagnostics(sce_spillr, "Yb173Di")
x_lim <- c(0, 7)
plot_grid(ps[[1]] + xlim(x_lim),
    ps[[2]] + xlim(x_lim),
    ncol = 1, align = "v"
)
